transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-02-12
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Acme PM), Priya Raman (Acme ML Eng), Carlos Mendes (Acme Infra)
- Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20250212-poc-67813

Summary:
Weekly POC sync focusing on caching improvements: prefix/KV cache hit rates, prompt reuse, and immediate tuning steps. Reviewed last week's benchmark (50k reqs), hit rates by route, discussed prompt templating to increase prefix reuse, agreed on next steps and who will run benchmarks and share traces.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick agenda — hit rates, prompt reuse, and next steps
[00:07] Jordan: thanks, yeah we've seen cost creep on the hosted flow so hoping caching helps. priya's got the data to show where reuse is low
[00:14] Priya: yep, i pulled a 48 hour sample, overall KV cache hit is around 21% on the main inference route, prefix cache is 18% — varies a lot by user cohort
[00:27] Samir: ok that's lower than ideal. can you share how you're constructing prompts? are you doing a lot of per-user personalization in the prefix?
[00:36] Priya: we do include user_name and last_action in the prompt prefix, and some session-specific metadata. some templates are nearly identical except for a token or two
[00:45] Carlos: also note our traffic has spikes at 9am and 17pm, we saw some cache churn when the index rotates
[00:53] Alex: right, two levers — template normalization to increase identical prefixes, and TTL/bucket tuning to reduce churn. samir, can you walk through the numbers from your run last week
[01:05] Samir: sure, ran 50k requests against hosted env with KV cache on. observed median latency down 8% overall when hit rate improved to 35% on a tuned route. cold start heavy routes still cost more. interestingly, our prefix cache gave diminishing returns beyond 40% due to TTL misalignment
[01:22] Priya: mmh, how are you measuring hits? we have a per-token and per-prefix metric — might be mixing them up
[01:29] Samir: good call. we instrument both. the dashboard shows prefix_hit_rate and kv_hit_rate; the semantical cache (prefix) counts only exact prefix matches after tokenization. kv cache counts KV cache lookups inside runtime for repeated k/v states
[01:44] Jordan: there's also prompt variability — different customers pass slightly different system prompts. can we standardize the system prompt?
[01:50] Alex: yes, that's low-hanging fruit. share a canonical system prompt, and use metadata tokens instead of verbatim phrases. Priya, could you try a quick A/B on templating for 10% traffic next week?
[01:59] Priya: yes we can. quick Q — will using metadata tokens break any downstream reranking? some of our post-processing expects exact strings
[02:07] Samir: you may need a light mapping layer in post. suggested approach: keep canonical tokens in the model input, then expand to full strings in postprocess. reduces prefix variance
[02:18] Carlos: network-wise, for dedicated or private we saw slightly better hit rates because requests stay on the same node pool, less KV eviction. but on hosted, cross-pool routing increases eviction pressure
[02:29] Alex: noted. one thing we can do immediately: increase bucket TTL for session-scoped prefixes from 5m to 15m for this cohort and measure. risk is stale personalization but we think it's acceptable for these intents
[02:42] Jordan: ok, what's the rollback plan if quality drops?
[02:45] Samir: we'll run canary with 10% traffic pinned to the optimized caching profile, run SLO checks — perplexity/metric comparisons and a manual sample review; if top-line quality delta > 2% or explicit failure cases appear we roll back TTL change
[02:58] Priya: for the templating experiment i'll create two prompt variants and mark them in the trace so you can compute delta quickly
[03:05] Alex: thanks. about instrumentation — Samir you said you pushed an updated dashboard, can you share link and the heatmap visualization
[03:13] Samir: yes, dashboard: https://redwood.app/dashboards/acme/poc-cache-heatmap and raw logs: https://redwood.app/logs/acme/poc-20250210. heatmap shows hot prefixes — top 20 prefixes cover 42% of hits. the long tail is problematic
[03:30] Jordan: interesting, can we precompute embeddings for those hot prefixes and store them? would that help?
[03:36] Samir: embedding precompute helps upstream caching decisions but doesn't replace prefix equality. if you can canonicalize the prefix text we get much higher raw hit rate which then uses cached KV state effectively
[03:48] Priya: we're concerned about PII in prefixes — we sometimes include user ids. any guidance on masking and still keeping cache effectiveness
[03:55] Alex: mask or hash user ids in the prompt, keep them out of canonical prefix. store user-scoped personalization in a separate token that isn't used for prefix matching. that's best practice
[04:06] Carlos: related infra note — we need to ensure KMS permissions for the dedicated nodes before running the benchmark, otherwise eviction spikes due to restarts will distort numbers
[04:15] Samir: noted, i'll coordinate with carlos on the nodes.
[04:20] Jordan: how much improvement should we expect with templating and TTL increase? any rough numbers?
[04:25] Samir: based on sim runs, templating alone could lift prefix hit 18 -> 45% for templated routes; combined with TTL tuning we saw up to 55% hit in the synthetic workload, cutting token spend ~27% on those routes
[04:39] Priya: that's promising. need to validate on our real traces though
[04:43] Alex: agreed, hence the 1h benchmark. also we'll produce a short checklist for the pilot: config, traces, nodes, dashboards, rollback criteria
[04:54] Jordan: can you email that checklist?
[04:56] Alex: yes i'll send after the call.
[04:58] Priya: one minor transcription note — i think the auto notes had "KV cash" in one place lol
[05:02] (laughter)
[05:05] Samir: quick technical deep-dive point — if you go to dedicated later, persisting the KV cache to node-local SSD between restarts gave us better warmup behavior in prior customers. worth considering for long pilots
[05:18] Carlos: hmm, we might prototype that on a small dedicated pool if the benchmark looks good
[05:22] Alex: ok let's recap next steps
[05:25] (recap)
[05:26] Alex: Samir runs 1h benchmark and shares the results and raw metrics dashboard; Alex sends the TTL + templating doc; Priya uploads traces and runs 10% A/B templating; Carlos verifies node/KMS config; team meets next Wednesday same time to review results
[05:44] Jordan: thanks all, appreciate it
[05:46] Alex: thanks everyone, bye
